issues.t: Head gasket leaks
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, the engine runs hot, a sweet coolant smell, or oil seeping from the sides of the engine.
issues.why: The non-turbo 2.5L boxer engines in these years are known for head gaskets that start seeping with age and mileage, either leaking oil outside or letting coolant escape.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and temperature gauge. If it starts running hot, pull over and have the cooling system pressure tested before driving further.

issues.t: Turbo oil supply pipe can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil smell or smoke from the engine bay, oil drips under the front of the car.
issues.why: On some turbocharged cars the oil feed pipe was assembled wrong and could crack, spraying oil onto hot parts with a risk of fire. Subaru recalled these cars to add a bracket and new pipe.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning oil or see smoke, stop and have it inspected before driving.

issues.t: Oil control valve cover bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking or a burning oil smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: Bolts holding an engine oil control valve cover could be loose, letting oil leak onto hot engine parts where it might catch fire. This was recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the bolts checked. Stop driving if you see smoke.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between changes and the low-oil light may come on before the next service.
issues.why: Early FB20 engines could burn oil past the piston rings. Owners were covered by a class settlement that paid for testing and repairs on qualifying cars.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and top up as needed. Ask a dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any coverage still applies.

issues.t: Valve springs can break (recall)
issues.sym: Ticking or clattering from the engine, rough running, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Some valve springs in the 2.0L engine could crack and break, which can make the engine run badly or stall. Subaru recalled the cars to replace the springs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the engine starts making new noises or runs rough, have it towed in rather than driving on.

issues.t: Engine computer can overheat ignition coils (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, misfires, rough running, or the engine stalling, sometimes with a blown fuse.
issues.why: A software fault let the engine computer keep powering an ignition coil after it should have stopped, which can damage the coil and cause a short. Subaru updated the software and replaced damaged coils.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both the original and the follow-up recall. If the engine stalls or misfires, have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: PCV valve can break apart inside the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, loss of power, or the engine shutting off while driving.
issues.why: The aluminum PCV valve could come apart and pieces could be pulled into the engine. Subaru recalled the cars and replaced the valve, or the whole engine if parts were missing.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have it done before more driving. If the engine loses power, pull over safely.

issues.t: Secondary air pump relay can stick on (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell from the front of the car, or a check engine light for the air injection system.
issues.why: On turbocharged models the relay for the secondary air pump could fail in the on position, letting the pump run until it overheats, with a risk of fire. Subaru replaced the relay.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you smell burning plastic after parking, have it checked right away.

issues.t: Fuel can leak at a hose joint on cold starts (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell, especially right after starting on cold mornings.
issues.why: On turbo WRX models fuel could seep where a fuel line joins a rubber hose when the engine was started cold, which is a fire risk. This was recalled.
issues.next: Do not ignore a fuel smell. Check the VIN for open recalls and have the fuel lines inspected.

issues.t: Engine may stall on winter-blend fuel (recall)
issues.sym: Rough idle, stalling, or trouble restarting, mainly in cold weather.
issues.why: Winter fuel with a high vapor rate could boil off in the fuel system and starve the engine. Subaru recalled the cars to fix it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for this recall and have it completed before cold weather.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, loss of power, or the engine stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: An impeller inside the fuel pump can swell and stick, so the pump stops delivering fuel. Subaru recalled the 2019 cars first and later added more years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the engine sputters or loses power, get off the road safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Automatic may not hold in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car creeps or rolls after being placed in Park.
issues.why: A faulty parking rod in the automatic transmission might not engage Park fully. This was recalled.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake and check the VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: CVT shudder, jerking or hesitation
issues.sym: Shudder or jerking at low speed, a bump when coming to a stop, hesitation, or stalling.
issues.why: Torque converter, fluid leak and control problems in early Lineartronic CVTs led Subaru to extend the transmission warranty on these years.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether software updates or repairs apply, and keep up with CVT fluid service.

issues.t: CVT shift cable nut may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter position may not match the gear the car is in, or the car may not shift as expected.
issues.why: A nut on the gear selector cable may not have been tightened at the factory and can work loose. Subaru recalled the cars to tighten it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Always set the parking brake until it is fixed.

issues.t: Driveshaft center support bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration, clunking under the car, or loss of drive power.
issues.why: Bolts holding the driveshaft center support could loosen, letting the front of the driveshaft come apart. This was recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Stop driving and have it towed if you feel strong vibration or lose drive.

issues.t: Front driveshaft joint can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking, vibration, or sudden loss of drive power. The car may roll if parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: The outer joint of the front driveshafts could crack and break. Subaru recalled the cars to replace them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and use the parking brake every time you park.

issues.t: Front lower control arms can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, wandering steering, or a front wheel sitting at an odd angle.
issues.why: In road-salt states the front lower control arm area could corrode badly enough to break. Subaru recalled cars from salt-belt states.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and check the VIN for an open recall. Do not drive if a wheel looks out of place.

issues.t: Front control arm weld can fail (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or a loose feel in the front end, steering pulling, or a wheel out of position.
issues.why: Some front lower control arms were built with a weak weld that could separate. Subaru told owners not to drive the car until the arm was replaced.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until the recall is done. Check the VIN and arrange a tow to the dealer if it is open.

issues.t: Brake lines can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stops, or brake fluid on the ground near a wheel.
issues.why: Salt spray in road-salt states could corrode the brake lines. Subaru recalled the cars, then ran a second campaign when the first fix was not enough.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have the brake lines inspected now and check the VIN: two campaigns were issued, because the first repair did not fully fix the problem.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder may not work right (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal travels further than normal before the car slows.
issues.why: A defect in the master cylinder could reduce braking, so more pedal travel was needed. Subaru recalled the cars for inspection.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the brakes inspected if the pedal feels long or soft.

issues.t: Brake light switch can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay off, the car will not shift out of Park, or push-button start will not work.
issues.why: Contamination can build up inside the brake light switch so it stops working. Subaru recalled the cars to replace the switch.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Ask someone to check your brake lights, and get it fixed quickly if they are out.

issues.t: Brake switch fault can disable EyeSight braking (recall)
issues.sym: EyeSight warnings, or automatic emergency braking not working.
issues.why: If the brake light switch fails, the pre-collision braking system could switch off. Subaru reprogrammed the system.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and do not rely on automatic braking until it is done.

issues.t: Brake switch may be out of adjustment (recall)
issues.sym: The car can start or shift out of Park without pressing the brake pedal, or the brake lights act oddly.
issues.why: The brake light switch could be set up wrong at the factory. Subaru recalled the cars to adjust it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and always hold the brake when starting and shifting.

issues.t: Cruise control cable can stick the throttle open (recall)
issues.sym: The car keeps accelerating or will not slow down after letting off the gas.
issues.why: The cruise control cable could slip off its lever and hold the throttle open. This was recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the throttle sticks, shift to neutral, brake firmly and pull over.

issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after a bump, and warning lights come on.
issues.why: A spring inside the ignition switch could break, letting the key move out of the Run position. That can stall the engine and may turn off the airbags. Subaru recalled the cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for this recall. Keep heavy items off the key ring until it is fixed.

issues.t: Remote starter fob can start the engine by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The engine starts on its own, for example after the key fob is dropped.
issues.why: On cars with a dealer-installed remote starter, the fob could send a start signal when knocked, which is dangerous in a closed garage. Subaru replaced the fobs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and do not leave the fob where it can be knocked while the car is in a garage.

issues.t: Headlights may be too dim (recall)
issues.sym: Poor light on the road at night even with working bulbs.
issues.why: The headlight reflectors may not reflect enough light. Subaru recalled the cars to fix the headlights.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and be careful driving at night until it is done.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may fail (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen stays blank or does not show the view behind the car.
issues.why: A software fault could stop the camera display from working. This was recalled for an update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and use mirrors and a shoulder check when backing up.

issues.t: Dash wiring can short and cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights and a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: A wiring harness behind the instrument panel could rub against a metal bracket and short out. Subaru recalled the cars to add a clamp and repair the wiring.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it done soon, since the car can lose power while driving.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light comes on with an adult in the seat, sometimes when a device is plugged in.
issues.why: The passenger seat sensor system could mistakenly turn off the passenger airbag. Subaru installed a modified control unit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Keep electronics unplugged from the front outlets until it is done.

issues.t: Pinched wire can disable passenger airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: Wiring for the passenger occupant sensor could be pinched and short, which may turn off the passenger airbag. This was recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the airbag light diagnosed.

issues.t: Driver seat bolt can fall out (recall)
issues.sym: The driver seat feels loose or rocks.
issues.why: A front bolt holding the driver seat to its rail could loosen and come out. This was recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the seat moves, have it fixed before driving.

issues.t: Wagon rear gate may drop (recall)
issues.sym: The rear hatch will not stay up or drops on its own.
issues.why: Bolts for the rear gate supports could be undertightened and a weld nut could break, letting the gate fall. This was recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and be careful under an open hatch until it is fixed.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. Some owners may notice wind noise or water around the windshield edge.
issues.why: Wrong clear paint coat on the body could keep the windshield adhesive from bonding, so the glass might not stay in place in a crash. Subaru recalled the cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it done promptly.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes, reboots or goes blank
issues.sym: The center screen locks up, restarts on its own, loses the radio or navigation, or drops the phone connection. The backup camera view can be affected when the screen is frozen.
issues.why: The Starlink head unit software in these years has known bugs. Subaru issued several bulletins with software updates for the head unit, and owners report some units being replaced.
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer to check the head unit software version and install the latest update. If the screen stays blank in reverse, get it looked at soon, since the backup camera depends on it.

issues.t: Wheel bearings wear out and start to howl
issues.sym: A humming, rumbling or growling from one corner of the car that rises and falls with road speed and often changes when you swerve gently from side to side. Owners of these years often report the same corner going bad again after a repair.
issues.why: The sealed bearings in the hubs on these early Imprezas have a short life, and water and road salt get past the seals. A bearing pressed in without the right tools, or a worn hub or axle left in place, wears the new bearing out quickly.
issues.next: Have the car put on a lift so the wheels can be checked for play and noise, and get the bad bearing replaced before it gets loose enough to upset the brakes or the steering. Ask the shop to check the hub and axle too, not just the bearing.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve covers, cam seals or crank seal
issues.sym: Oil drips under the car, a burning-oil smell after driving, oily residue on the sides or front of the engine, or a misfire and flashing check engine light when oil gets into the spark plug wells.
issues.why: On these boxer engines the valve cover gaskets, spark plug tube seals, front cam and crank seals and the oil cooler O-ring harden with heat and age. Oil then seeps onto the exhaust or pools around the spark plugs.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and top it up. Have a shop clean the engine and find the exact leak. Front seals are easiest to replace at the same time as the timing belt.

issues.t: Timing belt, tensioner or idler pulley failure
issues.sym: A whine, squeal or chirp from the front of the engine, or the engine suddenly quits while driving and cranks but will not start.
issues.why: These engines use a rubber timing belt that runs on a tensioner and idler pulleys. The pulleys and tensioner often wear out before the belt does. On the 2.5L and turbo engines a broken belt lets the valves hit the pistons.
issues.next: If the belt has not been changed on schedule (about every 105,000 miles or per your manual), have it replaced with the tensioner, pulleys and usually the water pump. If the engine dies and will not restart, tow it rather than keep cranking.

issues.t: Torn CV boots and clicking front axles
issues.sym: A clicking or popping noise when turning sharply, grease sprayed around the inside of a wheel, or a vibration when speeding up.
issues.why: The rubber boots that cover the axle joints crack with age and road debris. Grease leaks out and dirt gets in, so the joint wears and starts to click.
issues.next: Have the boots checked at oil changes. A torn boot caught early may only need a new axle; a clicking joint should be replaced before it fails.

issues.t: AWD binding or shudder in tight turns (automatic)
issues.sym: The car shudders, hops or feels like the brakes are dragging when turning sharply at low speed, such as in a parking lot.
issues.why: On the 4-speed automatic, a transfer clutch splits power between the front and rear wheels. If its control solenoid sticks or the clutch wears, the front and rear cannot turn at different speeds. Mismatched tire sizes or worn fluid make it worse.
issues.next: Make sure all four tires are the same size and evenly worn. Ask a shop about a transmission fluid change first, then testing the transfer solenoid. Avoid long drives with strong binding, which can damage the drivetrain.

issues.t: Rusty exhaust leaks, rattles or a P0420 code
issues.sym: A rattle or buzz from under the car, a louder exhaust, an exhaust smell, or a check engine light with a catalytic converter code (P0420).
issues.why: The exhaust pipes, flanges and heat shields rust, especially where roads are salted. A leak ahead of the oxygen sensor can confuse the engine computer and set a converter code even when the converter is fine.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected for leaks before replacing the catalytic converter. Do not ignore an exhaust smell inside the car.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. You may have received a recall letter about the front passenger airbag.
issues.why: The passenger airbag inflator can break apart when the airbag deploys and throw metal pieces into the cabin. Subaru issued several recall waves for these years.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls right away. The dealer replaces the inflator for free.

issues.t: Oil seeping from the cam carriers or timing chain cover
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil wetness on the sides or front of the engine, or a burning-oil smell from oil dripping onto the exhaust.
issues.why: The 2.0L engine is sealed with liquid sealant at the cam carriers and timing chain cover. With age that sealant can break down and let oil seep out. Subaru published a service bulletin on these leaks.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and ask a shop to confirm where the leak starts. Small seepage can be watched; a heavier leak needs resealing, which is a big job, so ask about warranty coverage on newer cars.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead while parked
issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting overnight or a few days, needs repeated jump-starts, or warning lights flicker and the engine stalls when auto start-stop kicks in.
issues.why: Some electronic modules, including the telematics (Starlink) module, may not fully go to sleep after the car is turned off. That slow drain flattens the battery. A 2026 lawsuit covers 2019-2023 Impreza, and Subaru issued a drain-testing bulletin for its gas models.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested, then ask the dealer to run a parasitic draw test and check for module software updates. Keep records of each dead battery.

issues.t: Infotainment screen goes black or keeps rebooting (warranty extension)
issues.sym: The center screen goes black or blank, sound cuts out, the unit reboots by itself, or CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, navigation or the touch screen stop working.
issues.why: The head unit itself can fail. Subaru extended coverage on these head units to 8 years or 150,000 miles (2019 cars are covered too).
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer to check for a software update first. If that does not fix it, the head unit is replaced while the extension applies. It may be covered.

issues.t: Screen stuck on "Starlink service update in progress"
issues.sym: The infotainment screen keeps showing a message that a Starlink service update is in progress, even after many drives.
issues.why: An over-the-air update to the telematics module failed partway. The message can stay on even after the module is replaced.
issues.next: This does not affect driving. Ask a Subaru dealer to reset the head unit memory and reload its software.

issues.t: Windshield cracks easily or with no clear impact
issues.sym: A small chip quickly spreads into a long crack, or a crack appears while parked or when the defroster is running.
issues.why: Owners of these years report windshields that crack from minor chips or with no clear cause. The Impreza is not part of the Subaru windshield settlement, so replacements are usually paid by the owner or insurance.
issues.next: Get chips repaired quickly. If you need a new windshield, make sure the EyeSight camera is recalibrated afterward. A crack in the driver view should be fixed before long trips.
